summary: Closed O-053. `CommandLine.JoinsNothingWindowsSplit` now treats an exposed token as an option only when it is exactly `--report`, which a new public `CommandLine.ReportOption` const names. App.xaml.cs reads the same const, so the two cannot drift. So `"D:\Data\" --report "C:\out --old\r.json"` repairs to [D:\Data\, --report, C:\out --old\r.json] instead of exiting 2. The review's test is at tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CommandLineDashFolderTests.cs unchanged and passes. The class is closed in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/UnpairedQuoteCorpus.json with 12 D rows, 1 R row and a dashSweep, and the old check fails those rows. The whole suite is 1451 of 1451 and the bug project 8 of 8.

files.why: Exposed-token check compares to the app's one option (`argument == ReportOption`) instead of `StartsWith("--")`; new public const ReportOption; docstring and comment corrected.
ReportOption now reads CommandLine.ReportOption, so the option spelling lives in one place.
The code review's failing test, verbatim.
Class corpus: rows D01-D12 and R01, and a dashSweep (tokens, rename, maxTokens).
New fact ADashedNameIsNeverTheReasonForADifferentVerdict: every line of up to 4 tokens is run as typed and with '--old' renamed to 'old', and the verdicts must match.
Exe-level fact AReportFolderWhoseNameStartsWithTwoDashesAfterASpaceIsTakenWhole (the Debug apphost exits 0 and writes the report at the exact path).

obligations.how: Replaced `argument.StartsWith("--")` with `argument == ReportOption` (a new public const in CommandLine; App reads the same one) in the exposed-token check, and corrected the docstring and comment. The review's test is at tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CommandLineDashFolderTests.cs verbatim and passes (2 of 2). The class is a corpus: UnpairedQuoteCorpus.json rows D01-D12 (dashed folders, several pieces, a bare '--', a name that is exactly '--report', a dashed piece after another argument, an argument absorbed into the piece, one dash, a dashed root, a dashed path ahead of the root, a stray quote with a dashed path) plus R01, which is still refused because the exposed '--report' would be hidden. The dashSweep runs 3,900 lines twice, as typed and with '--old' renamed to 'old', and requires the same verdict and the same elements. Before the fix, measured on the unfixed code: both CommandLineDashFolderTests rows fail (null), D01-D04 and D06-D08 fail (null), and the sweep fails 157 of 3,900 lines; D05, D09-D12 and R01 pass either way. After the fix all pass: the 39 CommandLine tests, the whole suite 1451 of 1451, and the bug project 8 of 8. The new exe fact exits 2 with the old check and 0 with the fix.

tests.note: Before: 4 of 5 fail. Both dash-test rows get null; corpus D01-D04 and D06-D08 are wrongly refused; the dash sweep fails 157 of 3,900 lines. Windows' own splits in every row's 'windows' field matched shell32.

tests.note: 1451 of 1451 (was 1448, +3: two dash-test rows and the dash sweep).

8 of 8 on the Debug apphost, started through its real entry point with a raw ProcessStartInfo.Arguments; includes the new fact on `"<tree>\" --report "<work>\out --old\r.json"`, which exits 0 and writes the report there with the right root and 3 files. Run again after restoring the fix from the mutant: 8 of 8.

tests.command: mutant: StartsWith("--") restored, then eng/dotnet.ps1 test <bug project> --filter AReportFolderWhoseNameStartsWithTwoDashes
tests.note: Red as it must be: the app exited with 2 on the dashed line. The fix was put back immediately and re-run green.

deviations: Added the public const CommandLine.ReportOption and made App.ReportOption read it. The obligation allowed `argument == "--report"` or a set of option names passed in; the App's option spelling is private to App.xaml.cs and Core cannot see it, so a second literal would be a copy that could drift.
follow_ups: The single-file published exe was not rebuilt for this attempt: the change is one string comparison in Core, and the Debug apphost exe facts (same code, real entry point) pass. Attempt 1 already measured the published exe on the repaired shapes.

A piece of a quoted report path that ends in a quote (a report path typed ending in a backslash, such as `"C:\out --old\"`) is still taken for a damaged root by the root branch of the exposed-token check and refused. That path is a folder, so the app would refuse the report path anyway (exit 3), and the obligation does not name it; filing it, not building it.
